ingredients: Dried millet/sorghum leaves (waakye leaves) or baking soda for color
Stew, gari, boiled egg, and spaghetti to serve
steps: Boil black-eyed peas with the waakye leaves (or a pinch of baking soda) until beans are almost tender and the water is reddish-brown.
Add washed rice to the same pot without draining the colored bean water.
Add salt and enough water to cook the rice through, covered, until tender.
Serve with a spicy stew, gari, boiled egg, and other accompaniments as desired.

ingredients: 1 kg fish (grouper or similar), cut into steaks
steps: Make the 'rof' stuffing by blending parsley, garlic, and chili; stuff into slits cut in the fish.
Sear the stuffed fish in oil until browned; set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions, add tomato paste and blended tomatoes, and cook until thickened.
Add water/stock and all vegetables, simmer until tender; remove and set aside with the fish.
Add the rice to the remaining broth and cook until tender, adding more liquid as needed.
Serve the rice topped with the fish and vegetables.

ingredients: 500g ndolé leaves (or substitute bitterleaf/spinach), washed well
steps: Boil the ndolé leaves (parboil and rinse well if using a bitter substitute) until tender; set aside.
Cook the mixed meats and smoked fish in stock until tender.
In a separate pot, sauté onion in oil, then stir in the ground peanut paste with a little water to loosen it.
Add the cooked meats, fish, shrimp, and their stock to the peanut mixture; simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the prepared ndolé leaves and simmer another 10-15 minutes until well combined.
Serve with boiled plantain, rice, or fufu.

ingredients: 2 large onions, thinly sliced and fried crispy
steps: Cook rice, lentils, and pasta separately until tender; keep warm.
Deep fry sliced onions until golden and crispy; set aside.
Make the tomato sauce: sauté garlic in oil, add blended tomatoes, cumin, vinegar, and simmer 15-20 minutes.
Make the chili vinegar sauce (dakka) by simmering garlic, vinegar, and chili together briefly.
Layer rice, lentils, pasta, and chickpeas in a bowl.
Top generously with tomato sauce, crispy onions, and chili sauce to taste.

ingredients: 1 kg lamb or chicken, cut into pieces
1 cup dried apricots or preserved lemon
steps: Heat oil in a tagine pot or heavy pan, brown the meat pieces on all sides.
Add onions and garlic, cook until softened.
Stir in ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, and saffron; cook briefly until fragrant.
Add stock, cover, and simmer gently for 1-1.5 hours until meat is very tender.
Add apricots or preserved lemon (and olives) in the last 15 minutes.
Serve hot directly from the tagine, with bread or couscous.
Sauté onion in olive oil until soft, then add turmeric and cinnamon.
Add vegetables and chickpeas, then pour in stock; simmer covered for 20-25 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile, steam or soak couscous according to package instructions, fluffing with a fork and a little oil.
Mound the couscous on a large plate, top with the vegetable stew and its broth.
Serve hot, traditionally shared from one large dish.
Sauté onion until soft, add curry powder and turmeric, cook briefly.
Add ground meat and cook through, then stir in soaked bread, raisins, and chutney.
Transfer to a baking dish and press down evenly; place bay leaves on top.
Whisk eggs with milk and pour over the meat mixture.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 35-40 minutes until the egg topping is set and golden.
Prepare a thick curry: sauté onions and garlic, add curry powder and turmeric, then meat and tomatoes.
Simmer covered until the meat is very tender and the sauce is thick (45-60 minutes).
Cut a quarter loaf of bread and hollow out the center, keeping the removed bread as 'lid' pieces.
Ladle the thick curry into the hollowed bread cavity.
Serve with the bread lid and a side of shredded carrot salad (sambal).
